notes: Direct translation. RL2's global.approvals.requiredSetValid becomes the state property ex:requiredApprovalSetValid; the four approvals, their binding to project P, their order, and their expiry are all computed by the approval service before the SOTW is frozen. Project P is prose in RL2 and is not a request parameter, so it is not modelled. RL2 says only that missing, expired, or conflicting approval evidence "does not establish the privilege"; due2 separates the cases. Expiry is assessed by the assembler and arrives as false (scenario 2: NotApplicable); missing or conflicting approval data arrives as a non-resolved status (scenarios 3 and 4: Indeterminate). Neither is Permit, so both agree with RL2's sentence. Scenarios 2–4 carry that sentence over; they have no rl2_expected because RL2 names no decision for them.

expected.why: The approval-set fact is true, so ex:approvedAccess is T; it has no duties and nothing prohibits.
The assembler found an expired approval and resolved the fact to false; false = true is F, so the permission is F and nothing else applies.
The fact is missing, so the permission is U; the completions give Permit and NotApplicable.
Two disagreeing values give status conflict, so the constraint is U; the completions give Permit and NotApplicable.
